chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿIsa and Musa ibn Jaʿfar, from Abi Jaʿfar, from Abi Talib ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid—and he is Dawud ibn Farqad—from some of our companions, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

When the sun passes the zenith, the time of Zuhr has entered, until there passes the amount of time in which a person praying can perform four rakʿahs. When that has passed, then the time of Zuhr and ʿAsr has entered, until there remains before sunset the amount of time in which a person praying can perform four rakʿahs. When that amount remains, then the time of Zuhr has ended, and the time of ʿAsr remains until the sun sets.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ: the length of time needed to perform four units of salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَغِيبَ: sets or disappears below the horizon

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Zuhr end and the exclusive time of ʿAsr begin?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the time boundaries of Zuhr and ʿAsr salat (prayer). It states that Zuhr begins at zawal, then after enough time for four rakʿahs both Zuhr and ʿAsr share the period, and when only enough time for four rakʿahs remains before sunset, Zuhr ends and only ʿAsr remains.
